messages.subject: Access Raw Data
messages.body_plain:

Thanks,
Shriya

messages.subject: Re: Access Raw Data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shriya,

the spectra() function should be valid. You can check the dimension of your loaded dataset by using dim().

This is the code I use to get the raw data matrix as txt file:

msidata_matrix = as.matrix(iData(msidata))

mz_names = paste0("mz_", mz(msidata))
pixel_names = paste0("xy_", coord(msidata)$x, "_", coord(msidata)$y)

 write.table(rbind(c("mz_name", pixel_names), cbind(mz_names, msidata_matrix)), ##create matrix
                    file="intensity_matrix.txt", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names=FALSE, sep = "\t")

Best,
Melanie

messages.subject: combining different runs with different numbers of features
messages.subject_clean: combining different runs with different numbers of features
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to using Cardinal (and new to analyzing DESI MS data) and am trying to combine three different runs together into one object using cbind().  I thus far have been unable to combine all three together because the number of rows (features) do not match.  I can combine run1 and run2 fine, but then I cannot combine run3 with them (run 3 has more features).  I have tried using mzBin() followed by process() like this:
AgNp1_bin <-mzBin(AgNp1_neg, from = 100, to = 1199.925, resolution=28, units="ppm)
AgNp1_bin <- process(AgNp1_bin)
AgNp2_bin <-mzBin(AgNp2_neg, from = 100, to = 1199.925, resolution=28, units="ppm)
AgNp2_bin <- process(AgNp2_bin)
AgNp3_bin <-mzBin(AgNp3_neg, from = 100, to = 1199.925, resolution=28, units="ppm)
AgNp3_bin <- process(AgNp3_bin)

cbind(AgNp1_bin, AgNp2_bin, AgNp3_bin)

 but I still get the error that the number of rows don't match.  I am sure it is likely a simple fix, but I am not quite sure what to do next.  Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks
Nadia

messages.subject: Re: Access Raw Data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Shriya,

yes with spectra() or iData() you obtain a table in which each line is one mz feature and each column one pixel and the content of the table are the intensities per mz feature and pixel.

You can find the code for obtaining an average mass spectra in section 6.5 of the user guide: http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/Cardinal/inst/doc/Cardinal-2-guide.html#summarization-e.g.-mean-spectra

Cheers,
Melanie

messages.subject: Re: Combine function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bailey,

the problem might be that you did not specify the resolution, which means that the optimal resolution will be calculated for each dataset and this probably resulted in (slightly) different values, thus leading to a differently binned m/z axis.
I assume just specifying a value for resolution should fix the problem. You can double check if the mz match after binning by using: all.equal(mz(mse_binned), mz(mse2_binned)). Please let us know in case the result is TRUE and cbind does still not work.

Best,
Melanie

messages.subject: Re: Processing/Normalization Speed Optimization
messages.body_plain:
The low CPU usage suggests it's an I/O issue. Are you using a computer with a traditional (spinning) hard drive? Data access will be quite slow in that case.

If you have enough memory, I'd suggest try using attach.only=FALSE to load the data fully and see if that helps.
